SPEECH.name: Speech structure
SPEECH.description: Hook the audience, make one clear point, support it, and end with a memorable close.
SPEECH.template: [An opening hook: a question, surprising fact or short story]. My main point is [your one key message]. For example, [evidence or a story that supports it]. To close, [a memorable final line].

STAR.name: STAR
STAR.description: Set the scene, state your responsibility, describe what you did, and finish with a measurable outcome.
STAR.template: The situation was [when and where this happened]. My task was [what you were responsible for]. So I [the specific steps you took]. As a result, [the outcome, ideally measurable], and I learned [the lesson you took from it].

PREP.name: PREP
PREP.description: Lead with your answer, justify it, back it with a concrete example, then restate it.
PREP.template: [Your answer in one sentence]. The reason is [why this is true for you]. For example, [a specific time it showed]. So, [restate your answer in a memorable way].

EXPLAIN.name: Explain simply
EXPLAIN.description: Start with the one-sentence idea, walk through the mechanism, ground it in an example, and close with the takeaway.
EXPLAIN.template: In simple terms, [the one-sentence idea]. It works like this: [the two or three key steps]. For example, [an everyday example]. This matters because [why the listener should care].

INTRO.name: Present-Past-Future
INTRO.description: Say who you are now, what in your background got you here, and where you want to go next.
INTRO.template: I'm [your name], currently [what you do now]. Before this, I [the education or experience that matters most]. Next, I want to [your goal], which is why [this role or opportunity] excites me.

PRESENT.name: Presentation flow
PRESENT.description: Grab attention, tell the audience what you'll cover, deliver the points with examples, then sum up with a call to action.
PRESENT.template: [A hook: a question, story or striking fact]. Today I'll cover [your two or three points]. First, [point one with an example]. Second, [point two with an example]. To sum up, [your key message], so [what you want the audience to do].

PITCH.name: Pitch
PITCH.description: Open with a hook, name the problem, show how you solve it, and finish with a specific ask.
PITCH.template: [A hook: a surprising fact or question]. The problem is [who struggles with what]. [You or your idea] solves it by [how]. So I'm asking for [a specific next step, such as a meeting or feedback].

ARGUE.name: Argument
ARGUE.description: State your stance, give your strongest reason, back it with evidence, and answer the other side.
ARGUE.template: I believe [your stance on the motion]. My main reason is [your strongest argument]. For example, [a fact, study or real case]. Some argue [the opposing view], but [why your position still holds].

modes.label: Free practice
modes.tagline: Speak about anything and get the full analysis.

coach.focus: General speaking practice. Judge whether the speaker makes a clear point and supports it.

modes.label: Interview
modes.tagline: Answer HR, behavioral, technical and self-introduction questions.

coach.focus: Job interview answer. Judge it like an experienced interviewer: does it answer the question directly, with specific evidence, in a well-organised way?

modes.label: JAM
modes.tagline: Just A Minute: talk for 60 seconds with no hesitation, repetition or deviation.

coach.focus: JAM (Just A Minute) round: the speaker must talk for one minute on the topic without hesitation, repetition or deviation. Reward creative, engaging ideas that stay on the topic.

modes.label: Snap talk
modes.tagline: Impromptu speaking: the topic appears, you get a few seconds to think, then talk.

coach.focus: Impromptu 'snap talk': the speaker had only a few seconds to prepare. Judge whether they quickly found one clear point and supported it, and be fair about the lack of preparation.

modes.label: Read aloud
modes.tagline: Read a news bulletin, announcement or story, or paste your own script.

modes.label: Presentation
modes.tagline: Present a topic within a target time, with optional notes to check coverage.

coach.focus: Presentation: judge the opening hook, whether the speaker signposts what they will cover, whether the key points are clear with examples, and whether it ends with a conclusion or call to action. If the speaker's outline is given, say which outline points were covered or missed.

modes.label: Pitch
modes.tagline: Elevator pitch: sell yourself or an idea in 30 or 60 seconds.

coach.focus: Elevator pitch: judge whether the first sentence hooks the listener, the problem and value are clear, and it ends with a specific ask. Brevity matters.

modes.label: GD / Debate
modes.tagline: Take a side on a motion and argue it, as in a group discussion or debate.

coach.focus: Group discussion or debate: the speaker argues {side} the motion. Judge how clear their stance is, the strength of their reasons and evidence, and whether they address the opposing view.
